name: FreeCAD (precise CAD)
description: Precise mechanical parts with FreeCAD's CAD kernel: exact holes for metal screws (clearance, self-tapping, heat-set inserts, nut traps, counterbores, countersinks — sizes from a table that prints well), slots, fillets, chamfers, hollow boxes; exact fit check between parts; STEP files for CNC / other CAD + STL for the printer.
about: Uses the FreeCAD installed on this PC (headless, its settings / macros / add-ons kept out). The AI only writes a recipe (data) — a fixed script builds it.
instructions:
FreeCAD = exact CAD for mechanical parts. Units mm, Z up.
FIRST: if the part is one of these READY-MADE designs, answer ONLY {"name": …, "template": …, "options": {…}} with just the options the user asked for (exact standard sizes are built in):
- motor_mount: a stepper motor mount. options: motor nema14|nema17|nema23, style l|flat, thickness, base_length, base_screw M3…M6, base_holes 2|4 (screws into the table), slots true (to tension a belt), gusset true|false.
- l_bracket: an angle bracket. options: width, leg_a (on the table), leg_b (up), thickness, screw, holes (per leg 1-4), countersink true|false, gusset true|false.
- enclosure: a box with a screwed-on lid (corner bosses with heat-set inserts). options: inner [w,d,h], wall, floor, lid, screw, fit insert|tap, corner (radius), board none|raspberry_pi_4|raspberry_pi_5|arduino_uno (adds its standoffs), standoff (height), cable_hole (diameter), vents true.
- mounting_plate: a flat plate with a grid of holes. options: size [w,d], thickness, screw, grid [nx,ny], margin, countersink true, center_hole (diameter), corner (radius).
- flange: a round flange for a shaft. options: outer_diameter, thickness, bore (shaft), bolt_circle, bolts (count), screw, hub_diameter, hub_height, set_screw true.
- spacer: a standoff. options: screw, length, outer_diameter, hex true, fit clearance|tap|insert.
- pipe_clamp: a 2-piece clamp around a pipe. options: pipe_diameter, width, wall, screw.
OTHERWISE (template none) give bodies. One BODY per separate part (a box + its lid = 2 bodies); "reference": true on bought parts that are only shown.
PARTS build a body in order: the first is the start, then "op" add / cut / intersect. Every shape's "center" is its MIDDLE. box: size [x,y,z] (+ "round": radius for rounded vertical corners). cylinder / cone / tube: radius (cone: radius2), height, axis x|y|z, tube: wall. sphere: radius. slot (a long round-ended hole): length, width, height = depth, axis = the direction it goes INTO the part, direction = along its length. polygon: points [[x,y],…] (outline seen from above) extruded by height. rotate [x,y,z] degrees. Parts of ONE body must touch or overlap.
HOLES — the easy way: put them on a FACE of a part: {"face": "top", "part": 1, "pos": [u, v]} = on the top face of the body's first part, pos measured from that face's CENTRE (top / bottom: u = x, v = y; front / back: u = x, v = z; left / right: u = y, v = z). The app finds the surface and drills INTO the part. (Or "at" [x,y,z] on the surface + "axis" -z|+z|-x|+x|-y|+y.) depth in mm, 0 = through. For METAL SCREWS give "for" (M2…M10) and "fit": clearance (passes) / tap (cuts its thread) / insert (brass heat-set) / nut (hexagon pocket) — the app knows the exact sizes; "head": counterbore | countersink. Other holes: "diameter". Many holes: "pattern": {"grid": [2,2], "step": [40,30]} (starting at the hole) or {"circle": 6, "radius": 25} (around it).
EDGES: "fillet": radius (vertical outer edges; fillet_edges top|all), "chamfer": size (bottom edges by default). "shell": wall = hollow with an open top — ONLY for boxes / containers.
Print-friendly: walls 2+ mm, 2.5 mm around screw holes, assembly gaps 0.3-0.4 mm.
Example (custom): {"name": "sensor holder", "template": "none", "bodies": [{"name": "holder", "parts": [{"shape": "box", "size": [50, 20, 4], "center": [0, 0, 2], "round": 3}, {"shape": "box", "size": [20, 4, 30], "center": [0, -8, 15]}], "holes": [{"face": "top", "part": 1, "pos": [-17, 0], "for": "M3", "fit": "clearance", "head": "countersink", "pattern": {"grid": [2, 1], "step": [34, 0]}}, {"face": "front", "part": 2, "pos": [0, 8], "diameter": 12}]}]} Holes with a "dir" and parts with a "thread" were made by the user by hand in Create › 3D: keep them exactly as they are (same numbers) unless the user asks to change them. fit_test: the micro-gauge — pegs + holes 0.0-0.4 mm bigger (options: diameter 10, peg_height 8): one 15-minute print tells the printer's real fit; pick it for "fit test", "tolerance test", "what clearance does my printer need".
